text:
maria: Heads-up: getting a batch of customer reports about 5xx from the hosted API since 09:12 UTC. Most are 502/504 gateway errors. Looks correlated to control-plane calls. Investigating now.

ashley: saw the spike in the error budget dashboard. 5xx rate jumped from 0.3% -> 6% at 09:11. Latency to routing-policy svc also increased.

sanjay: +1, from infra logs it looks like config-db timeouts started at 09:10. Queries to /policy/select were spiking and timing out at ~5s.

maria: customer repro: simple generation call to hosted API returns 502 with body: `\{"error":"upstream request failed"\}`. Repro steps I used: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-13b\",\"input\":\"hi\"}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate` -> intermittent 502.

raj: tagging in eng-sre-oncall: @eng-sre-oncall can you confirm if any deployments or DB ops happened around 09:05-09:15?

eng-sre-oncall: looking. No config deploys. There was a brief autoscaler activity 09:07-09:09 but nominal. I'm pulling control-plane logs now (routing-policy and auth-session).

deploy-bot: [deploy] no active deploys in support or controlplane namespaces in last 6 hours.

ashley: dashboard snippets:
```
controlplane.routing_policy.latency_p50: 120ms -> 2.3s
controlplane.routing_policy.errors_5xx: 0.2% -> 4.7%
configdb.connection_errors: spike at 09:10 -> 200/s
```

sanjay: tail from controlplane router logs:
```
2026-03-14T09:10:12Z ERROR route-eval timeout: config-db read timed out (deadline exceeded)
2026-03-14T09:10:13Z WARN fallback to default-route
2026-03-14T09:10:14Z ERROR auth: session fetch failed: rpc error: code=Unavailable desc=transport is closing
```

maria: customers report billing/invoice API calls also impacted? or just inference? One premium customer says their embed pipeline got 502s.

raj: likely systemic — routing-policy fetches session+policy per request. If config DB is hanging that can cascade into auth/session and produce gateway 502s from the control plane.

eng-sre-oncall: I see the config-db pod CPU at 98% and a connection storm from ~09:09 coming from routing-policy replicas. Possibly a slow query or an index regression. Spawning a read-replica to absorb reads, and temporarily increasing DB connection pool.

ashley: can we add a short-term mitigation: enable routing-policy local cache TTL to 30s and increase auth-session cache TTL to avoid chattiness? That should cut DB QPS immediately.

eng-sre-oncall: applying cache TTL policy now (rolling to 3 replicas). Patch command: `kubectl patch configmap controlplane-cache --type merge -p '{"data":{"policy_ttl":"30s","session_ttl":"45s"}}'`

maria: applied, monitoring customer reports. Also sending a short note to affected customers via status page. (cc: @support-team) :loudspeaker:

raj: also throttling ingress for heavy customers for 10m to reduce burst. I added a temporary route rule in the API gateway to soft-limit concurrent requests from customers with >10k/s usage.

eng-sre-oncall: read-replica came up at 09:19, connection errors subsided by 09:20. Rolling latencies back to normal by 09:22. Config DB CPU down to 45%.

sanjay: confirmed in traces: routing-policy p50 dropped back to 140ms by 09:23. 5xx rate returning to baseline.

maria: customer follow-ups: some saw partial failures but most recovered after 09:22. I'm keeping incident open until 2 hours after stabilization and will collect postmortem details.

ashley: action items: 1) investigate slow query in config DB (probable missing index) 2) run a load test to reproduce storm pattern 3) add circuit-breaker so control-plane returns 429 rather than 502 when config-db is degraded 4) tune default cache TTLs to be more defensive.

raj: I'll take (1) with DB. sanjay you own (2) load-test. ashley can you draft the circuit-breaker proposal and coords for a rollback strategy?

eng-sre-oncall: final status: mitigated. Monitoring for any regression for next 2 hours. Marking incident as triaged.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll post a short summary to #incidents and create a ticket in postmortems for root cause + follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
